task.instruction:
Allocate a clinic's transport contract when the highest-capacity bid omits a required access service.

Select one bid, allocate the full contract, and state the binding eligibility threshold.

evidence.content: Bid Amber offers 1,200 monthly rides for $90,000 but provides no wheelchair-accessible vehicles.
Bid Blue offers 1,050 monthly rides for $96,000 and guarantees 120 wheelchair-accessible rides.
The clinic has $100,000 and 83 registered patients require wheelchair-accessible transport.
The procurement specification requires accessible transport for every registered patient who needs it.

target_a.content:
Situation: A cooling-center program has one additional bus during a five-day heat warning.
Evidence:
[history-01-e1] Route Ridge serves 70 medically vulnerable residents who have no other transport.
[history-01-e2] Route Central serves 210 residents, 160 of whom can also reach rail; a contracted reserve guarantees booking capacity for all 70 Ridge residents and achieved 96% on-time completion, above the program's 95% service floor, while the dedicated bus achieved 99%.
Decision: Assign the bus to Route Ridge and publish the medical-need rule.
Reasoning: The dedicated route preserves the larger safety margin for residents with no alternative transport.

Situation: A support center can spend its final 40 staff-hours on severe old cases or a common issue affecting many customers.
Message: We considered [history-02-e1] Twenty severe cases have waited nine days and each requires two hours to resolve. [history-02-e2] A shared fix would resolve the common issue for 180 customers but would leave the severe cases waiting three more days. The decision is Resolve the twenty severe nine-day cases before the shared fix.
Reasoning: The oldest high-severity cases should not fall below a defensible service floor to improve the total count.

Situation: A school has 60 tutoring-hours for either individual support or a group workshop.
Record: [history-03-e1] Ten learners below the required reading floor need six individual hours each to reach the next assessed step. [history-03-e2] A group workshop can give 60 learners one hour of exam practice and is expected to improve average scores modestly; the next individual-support block starts in four weeks, before the final assessment but after two graded assignments, and can cover all ten learners.
Recorded decision: Use the hours to bring the ten learners to the required reading floor.
Reasoning: A broad average gain does not substitute for the minimum capability the program guarantees.

situation=A regional water utility can restore backup capacity for one fragile line or improve pressure across the larger network. evidence=[history-04-e1] Restoring the backup pump for the fragile line serves 380 residents, costs 48 maintenance-hours, and removes a single point of failure after two recent outages. [history-04-e2] A network pressure tune-up costs the same 48 hours and is expected from prior work to improve service for 8,400 households; the next backup-pump slot is in three weeks before the forecast high-demand period. decision=Restore the fragile line's backup pump before the network-wide tune-up.
Reasoning: The smaller line should not remain without a recovery path in exchange for a broader average improvement.

Situation: A platform has budget for either one fragile critical service or a broad efficiency update.
Evidence:
[history-05-e1] The critical service supports 4% of users but has no failover and experienced two six-hour outages last quarter.
[history-05-e2] The efficiency update reduces average page latency by 12% for all users and has no effect on the critical service; the next budget window for failover opens in six weeks.
Decision: Fund failover for the fragile critical service.

Situation: A rationing proposal increases total appointments by excluding patients who require an interpreter.
Message: We considered [history-06-e1] Interpreter access is a required eligibility accommodation for 28 registered patients. [history-06-e2] A compliant schedule serves 12 fewer total appointments but preserves interpreter slots. The decision is Reject the exclusion and use the compliant schedule with interpreter slots.

Situation: A grant formula appears to serve more applicants but hides a new residency restriction from the published rules.
Record: [history-07-e1] The restriction would exclude 14 eligible applicants under the current public criteria. [history-07-e2] The formula can be rerun under the published rule before awards are due.
Recorded decision: Reject the hidden restriction and rerun the formula under the published eligibility rule.

situation=A routine service request fits the published rule and available capacity covers every eligible applicant. evidence=[history-08-e1] All 34 requests satisfy the same documented eligibility criteria. [history-08-e2] The program has 40 available slots and no protected service need is displaced. decision=Approve all 34 requests under the published rule.
